Mix the flour, yeast, water and salt into a soft dough, knead for 10 minutes and leave to rise for 2 hours.
Crush the tomatoes by hand with the garlic, a pinch of salt and 1 tbsp oil.
Divide into 3 balls, rest 30 minutes, then stretch each into a thin round with a thicker rim.
Spread with tomato, add mozzarella and bake on a very hot stone or tray at the highest oven heat for 7 to 9 minutes.
Finish with basil and a drizzle of oil.
Fry the fresh mushrooms in the oil until golden and set aside.
Soften the onion and garlic in half the butter, add the rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the chopped porcini, then the porcini liquid and stock a ladle at a time for 18 minutes, stirring.
Stir in the fried mushrooms, remaining butter and parmesan and rest 2 minutes.
Fry the garlic and chilli gently in the oil for 2 minutes.
Add the passata and salt and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook the penne until al dente.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and a splash of pasta water.
Toast the pepper in a dry pan for 1 minute.
Cook the pasta in less water than usual, salted lightly, and keep 300 ml of the starchy water.
Mix the cheese with a few spoons of warm pasta water to a smooth paste.
Add the pasta to the pepper pan with a ladle of water off the heat, then stir in the cheese paste quickly.
Toss until creamy, adding water as needed, and serve at once.
Soften the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the beef and brown, then the tomato paste.
Add the milk and let it bubble away, then the passata and stock.
Simmer on low for 1.5 hours, stirring now and then, until rich.
Cook the spaghetti, toss with the sauce and serve with parmesan.
Blend the basil, pine nuts, garlic, parmesan, oil and salt to a bright sauce.
Boil the gnocchi until they float, about 2 minutes.
Toss with the basil sauce and tomatoes, loosening with the water.
Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil for 1 minute.
Add the mussels, clams, grape juice and lemon, cover and cook for 4 minutes until they open, discarding any closed ones.
Add the squid, prawns and tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Cook the linguine 1 minute short of al dente and finish it in the sauce for 1 minute.
Fry the cumin seeds in the oil, add the chicken and ginger garlic paste and cook on high for 5 minutes.
Add the ground spices and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the onion, peppers and chillies and stir-fry for 4 minutes so they stay crunchy.
Sprinkle with garam masala and season.
Fry the onion in half the butter for 6 minutes, add the ginger garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomato purée, cashews and chilli and simmer for 12 minutes, then blend smooth.
Return to the pan with the remaining butter, garam masala, honey and salt.
Stir in the cream and crushed fenugreek.
Add the paneer and simmer 3 minutes, then serve with naan.
Rub the prawns with turmeric and salt and sear in 1 tbsp ghee for 1 minute, then remove.
Fry the cinnamon and cardamom in the remaining ghee, add the onion purée and cook for 6 minutes.
Add the ginger garlic paste, chilli and green chillies for 2 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk with the sugar and simmer for 5 minutes, then add the prawns for 3 minutes.
Sprinkle with garam masala and serve with rice.
Blend the chillies, garlic, ginger, whole spices and vinegar to a smooth paste.
Marinate the beef in two-thirds of the paste with salt for at least 2 hours.
Fry the onions in the oil until golden, add the remaining paste and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the beef and sugar and sear, then 400 ml water, cover and simmer for 90 minutes until tender.
Reduce until the sauce is thick and serve with rice.
Soften the onion, garlic and pepper in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, bay leaves and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the olives, capers and jalapeños.
Lay the seasoned fish in the sauce, cover and simmer for 8 minutes until it flakes.
Toss the chicken with the spices, juice of one lime, 1 tbsp oil and salt.
Sear the chicken in a very hot skillet for 6 minutes and remove.
Cook the peppers and onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until charred.
Return the chicken and toss together.
Serve sizzling with warm tortillas, sour cream, avocado and lime.
Poach the chicken in the stock for 15 minutes and shred.
Boil the tomatillos, jalapeños, half the onion and garlic for 8 minutes, then blend with coriander, salt and some stock for green sauce.
Soften the tortillas in hot oil for a few seconds each.
Roll the chicken in the tortillas and lay in a dish, then pour over the sauce.
Bake at 190°C for 15 minutes and top with cheese, sour cream and sliced onion.
Blend the chillies, tomatoes, garlic, cumin, oregano, salt and 300 ml soaking water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Brown the beef with half the onion and season with a few spoons of sauce.
Dip each tortilla in the sauce, fill with beef and roll.
Lay in a dish, pour over the remaining sauce and top with cheese.
Bake at 190°C for 15 minutes and serve with sour cream and onion.
Poach the chicken in the stock with salt for 30 minutes and keep the stock.
Toast the chillies briefly, soak in hot water for 15 minutes, and fry the almonds, half the sesame, raisins and tortilla in the oil until golden.
Blend everything with the tomatoes, onion, garlic, spices and some stock to a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in a pot for 10 minutes, stirring, then add the chocolate, sugar and stock to make a thick velvety sauce.
Add the chicken, simmer 10 minutes and sprinkle with the remaining sesame.
Simmer the beef in water with salt for 2 hours until it shreds, keeping the broth.
Blend the chillies, garlic, cumin and some broth and mix with the shredded beef.
Beat the oil with the masa harina, baking powder, salt and enough warm stock to make a soft spreadable dough.
Spread dough on each husk, add beef, fold and stand upright in a steamer.
Steam for 75 minutes until the dough pulls away from the husk.
Blend the chillies, achiote, pineapple juice, garlic, vinegar, cumin and salt and marinate the beef for 2 hours.
Sear the beef in batches in the hot oil until charred, then chop.
Char the pineapple in the same pan.
Fill with beef and pineapple and top with onion, coriander and lime.
Simmer the beef with half the onion and salt for 2 hours until tender, then shred and crisp in a hot pan.
Blend the tomatoes, remaining onion, garlic and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes for a mild sauce.
Blend the chillies with vinegar, salt and water for the hot sauce.
Spread the rolls with beans and fill with beef.
Pour the tomato sauce over and hot sauce to taste, and top with pickled onion.
Poach the chicken in the stock for 15 minutes and shred.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic and one chilli, fry in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes and add to the stock with epazote.
Fry the tortilla strips and the remaining chilli in oil until crisp.
Serve the soup over chicken and tortilla strips with avocado, cheese, sour cream and lime.
Blend the achiote, orange and lime juices, garlic, cumin, oregano and salt and marinate the beef overnight.
Wrap in banana leaves in a dish, pour over the marinade and cover with foil.
Cook at 160°C for 3.5 hours until it falls apart.
Pickle the red onion with habanero, lime and salt.
Shred the beef in its juices and serve in tortillas with the pickled onion.
Dip the chicken in seasoned flour, egg, then breadcrumbs mixed with half the parmesan.
Fry in 4 tbsp oil for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Simmer the passata with garlic, basil, the remaining oil and salt for 10 minutes.
Put the chicken in a dish, spoon over some sauce, top with mozzarella and the rest of the parmesan and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes.
Serve with spaghetti tossed in the remaining sauce.
Lay a slice of turkey and two sage leaves on each escalope and secure with a toothpick.
Season lightly and dust the underside with flour.
Fry in the oil and half the butter, sage side down first, for 2 minutes per side.
Remove, add the stock and lemon juice to the pan and reduce for 2 minutes, then swirl in the remaining butter.
Pour the sauce over the beef and serve with potatoes or greens.
Brown the beef in the oil, add the onion, carrot, celery and garlic for 8 minutes, then the tomato paste and passata, and simmer for 40 minutes.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and cook until thick, then season with nutmeg and salt.
Layer ragù, lasagne sheets, béchamel and mozzarella in a dish, three times.
Finish with béchamel, mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until golden and rest 10 minutes before cutting.
Simmer the passata with the oil, garlic, basil and salt for 10 minutes.
Boil the gnocchi for 2 minutes until they float and drain.
Toss the gnocchi with the sauce in a baking dish.
Top with the mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake at 210°C for 15 minutes until bubbling and golden, then scatter with basil.
Soften the onion, fennel and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and chilli flakes for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and stock, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the fish and mussels, cover and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until the mussels open and the prawns are pink, discarding any closed mussels.
Season, scatter with parsley and serve with toasted bread.
Season the chicken, dust with flour and fry in the oil for 4 minutes per side until golden, then set aside.
Add the butter, mushrooms and shallots and cook for 6 minutes until browned, then add the garlic.
Pour in the grape juice and balsamic vinegar and reduce by half.
Add the stock, return the chicken and simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce is glossy.
Finish with parsley and serve with mashed potatoes or pasta.
Salt the eggplant slices for 20 minutes, pat dry and fry or brush with oil and roast at 200°C for 20 minutes until golden.
Simmer the passata with garlic, a little oil, basil and salt for 15 minutes.
Layer sauce, eggplant, mozzarella and parmesan in a baking dish, repeating three times.
Finish with sauce and parmesan and bake at 190°C for 30 minutes until bubbling.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes, and keep a cup of the water.
Fry the turkey rashers in the oil for 6 minutes until crisp.
Whisk the yolks, egg, pecorino and black pepper.
Toss the pasta and peas with the turkey off the heat, then stir in the egg mixture with splashes of pasta water until silky.
Dust the beef with seasoned flour and brown in 2 tbsp oil, then soften the onion, carrot and celery in the same pot.
Add the grape juice, tomatoes and 300 ml stock, return the beef, cover and braise on low for 90 minutes.
For the risotto, toast the rice in the remaining oil, then add the rest of the stock with water and the saffron a ladle at a time for 18 minutes, stirring, and finish with parmesan.
Chop the parsley, lemon zest and garlic together to make gremolata.
Serve the beef on the risotto with its sauce and a sprinkle of gremolata.
Dust the beef with seasoned flour and brown in 2 tbsp oil, then soften the onion, carrot and celery in the same pot.
Add the grape juice, tomatoes and 300 ml stock, return the beef, cover and braise on low for 90 minutes.
For the risotto, toast the rice in the remaining oil, then add the rest of the stock with water and the saffron a ladle at a time for 18 minutes, stirring, and finish with parmesan.
Chop the parsley, lemon zest and garlic together to make gremolata.
Serve the beef on the risotto with its sauce and a sprinkle of gremolata.
Dust the beef with seasoned flour and brown in 2 tbsp oil, then soften the onion, carrot and celery in the same pot.
Add the grape juice, tomatoes and 300 ml stock, return the beef, cover and braise on low for 90 minutes.
For the risotto, toast the rice in the remaining oil, then add the rest of the stock with water and the saffron a ladle at a time for 18 minutes, stirring, and finish with parmesan.
Chop the parsley, lemon zest and garlic together to make gremolata.
Serve the beef on the risotto with its sauce and a sprinkle of gremolata.
Season and flour the chicken, then fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side and set aside.
Add the garlic, then the stock and lemon juice and reduce for 4 minutes.
Add the capers, return the chicken and simmer for 2 minutes, then swirl in the butter.
Cook the pasta for 3 minutes and drain.
Serve the chicken over the pasta with the sauce and parsley.
Soften the onion, carrots and celery in the oil for 8 minutes, add the zucchini for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook for 8 minutes, then stir in the spinach until wilted.
Mash the garlic with the butter, spread on sliced baguette and bake at 200°C for 8 minutes until crisp.
Serve the soup with parmesan and the garlic bread.
Mix the paneer, potato, cornflour and salt, shape into 12 balls and deep-fry for 4 minutes until golden.
Soak the cashews in hot water for 10 minutes.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the butter for 8 minutes, add the tomatoes and spices and cook for 10 minutes.
Blend the sauce with the cashews until smooth and return to the pan with the cream, sugar and salt.
Simmer 3 minutes, pour over the koftas just before serving.
Marinate the chicken in yogurt with half the garam masala, turmeric, chilli and salt for 20 minutes, then grill or sear for 8 minutes until charred.
Cook the rice with the cumin seeds, 1 tbsp oil and salt in 600 ml water for 15 minutes.
Fry the onion in the remaining oil for 8 minutes, add garlic and ginger, then tomatoes and the remaining garam masala, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the chicken and cream and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve over the cumin rice with fresh coriander.
Pressure-cook or simmer the drained lentils and beans in 1.2 l water with salt for 60 minutes until completely soft.
Melt half the butter, fry the onion for 8 minutes, then the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the tomato purée and chilli powder and cook for 8 minutes until the butter separates.
Add the lentils with their liquid and simmer on low for 30 minutes, stirring and mashing a little.
Stir in the remaining butter, cream, garam masala and crushed fenugreek and serve with naan or rice.
Simmer the lentils in 1 l water with turmeric for 25 minutes until soft, then whisk smooth.
Add the tomato and salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Fry the onion in half the ghee for 6 minutes and stir it into the dal.
Heat the remaining ghee, fry the cumin, garlic, chillies and asafoetida until sizzling and the garlic is golden.
Pour the tempering over the dal and finish with coriander and a squeeze of lemon.
Fry the onions in the oil for 10 minutes, add the mutton and ginger garlic paste and sear for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook for 5 minutes.
Add 500 ml water, cover and simmer for 60 minutes until tender.
Blanch and purée the spinach with the green chillies.
Stir in the spinach and garam masala and cook uncovered for 10 minutes.
Fry the onions in the ghee for 15 minutes until deep golden, remove half for the topping.
Add the lamb, garlic, ginger, yogurt, biryani masala, chilli, turmeric, half the herbs and salt and cook covered for 45 minutes until tender.
Boil the rice with cardamom, bay leaves and salt for 6 minutes until three-quarters cooked and drain.
Layer the rice over the lamb, scatter the remaining herbs and fried onions and drizzle the saffron milk.
Seal with a lid and cook on very low heat for 20 minutes, then fluff gently and serve.
Rub the chicken with lemon juice, salt and chilli and leave 15 minutes.
Coat in yogurt mixed with ginger garlic paste, cumin, garam masala and oil and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Roast at 230°C on a rack for 30 minutes, turning once, until charred and cooked through.
Serve with onion, tomato and cucumber salad.
Heat the ghee and fry the whole spices and bay leaves for 1 minute.
Add the lamb and sear over high heat for 8 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt with the chilli powder and add it gradually, stirring, then add the asafoetida.
Add the fennel, ginger, salt and 400 ml hot water, cover and simmer for 75 minutes until the lamb is very tender.
Uncover and reduce for 5 minutes until the red oil rises, then serve with rice.
Marinate the chicken in yogurt, half the chilli, ginger garlic paste, half the garam masala and salt for 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear the chicken for 10 minutes until charred and cooked.
Melt the butter, add the tomato purée, remaining chilli and garam masala, and simmer for 12 minutes.
Stir in the cream, honey, crushed fenugreek and the chicken, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Cook the rice and serve with the butter chicken.
Fry the whole spices in the oil for 1 minute, then the onions for 15 minutes until deep brown.
Add the garlic, ginger and chillies, then the beef, and fry over high heat for 10 minutes to sear.
Add the ground spices, tomatoes and salt and stir well.
Cover and cook on low for 50 minutes, adding a splash of water only if it sticks.
Uncover and fry (bhuna) for 10 minutes until the masala clings to the meat, then sprinkle with garam masala.
Blanch the spinach for 2 minutes, cool in cold water and blend to a smooth purée.
Fry the paneer in 1 tbsp ghee until lightly golden and set aside.
Fry the cumin seeds in the remaining ghee, then the onion for 6 minutes, then garlic, ginger, chilli and tomato for 4 minutes.
Add the spinach purée, garam masala and salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream and paneer, heat through and serve with roti or rice.
Fry the cumin seeds in the oil, then the onion for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli for 1 minute, then the ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until thick.
Add the chickpeas, anardana, salt and 250 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken.
Finish with fresh coriander and serve with rice or bread.
Fry the mustard seeds and curry leaves in the oil until they pop, then the onion for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the ground spices, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir to coat for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tamarind and salt and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk, simmer 5 minutes more and serve with rice.
Heat the oil and fry the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the ginger, garlic and chilli for 1 minute, then the turmeric and ground coriander.
Add the potatoes and cauliflower with salt and toss to coat, then cover and cook on low for 12 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook uncovered for 8 minutes, stirring gently, until the vegetables are tender.
Sprinkle with garam masala and fresh coriander and serve.
Marinate the chicken with yogurt, ginger garlic paste, spices, lemon juice, half the herbs, half the fried onions and salt for at least 30 minutes.
Spread the marinated chicken in a heavy pot with 2 tbsp ghee.
Boil the rice with cardamom, cinnamon and salt for 6 minutes until 70% cooked and drain.
Layer the rice over the chicken with the remaining herbs, onions, saffron milk and ghee.
Seal the lid and cook on high for 5 minutes, then on very low for 40 minutes, rest 5 minutes and serve.
Fry the onions in the ghee for 12 minutes until golden, then blend with the cashews and a splash of water to a smooth paste.
Fry the whole spices in the pan for 1 minute, add the ginger garlic paste and chicken and cook for 6 minutes.
Add the onion paste, yogurt, coriander and salt and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut cream and saffron and simmer 5 minutes more.
Toast the almonds and scatter over before serving with rice.
